subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and current color-system best practices (OKLCH/LCH perceptual uniformity, WCAG 2.1 / APCA contrast, semantic tokens, light/dark parity, color-vision-deficiency safety).

cases.scenario: A team is starting a design system. A designer hand-picked a 10-step gray scale by eye in HSL by stepping lightness in even 10% increments; the mid-tones look bunched and the light end looks washed out.
cases.context: The product needs even, predictable scales for borders, surfaces, and text across many components.
cases.question: How should the agent build the scale?
expected_flags: Generate the scale in OKLCH/LCH, not HSL — equal HSL lightness steps are perceptually uneven
Equal step indices should have equal lightness within ~±2 L units
Anchor the brand/seed at a defined step and derive the rest by rule rather than eyeballing
Export to sRGB or display-p3 with fallbacks
expected_fix_hints: Regenerate the scale programmatically in oklch() with even L steps
Map each step to a numbered token (50..900)
absent_signals: Do not keep hand-tuning HSL lightness percentages
Do not eyeball individual mid-tones to fix the bunching

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Generate the scale in OKLCH/LCH, not HSL — equal HSL lightness steps are perceptually uneven.
Surfaces this expected flag: Equal step indices should have equal lightness within ~±2 L units.
Surfaces this expected flag: Anchor the brand/seed at a defined step and derive the rest by rule rather than eyeballing.
Surfaces this expected flag: Export to sRGB or display-p3 with fallbacks.

Recommends this expected fix or action: Map each step to a numbered token (50..900).
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep hand-tuning HSL lightness percentages.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not eyeball individual mid-tones to fix the bunching.

cases.scenario: A palette uses a #9CA3AF gray for secondary text on a white surface and a brand-blue button label in #FFFFFF on a #4DA3FF background. Accessibility QA reports several pairings feel hard to read.
cases.context: The product must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the team wants a token-level fix, not per-page patches.
cases.question: How should the agent audit and fix the contrast?
expected_flags: Compute WCAG 2.1 contrast ratios for each text/background pair against the AA floor (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large)
Both example pairs likely fail AA for normal text; darken the gray / deepen the button background or shift label
Fix at the semantic-token level so the correction propagates everywhere
Add an automated AA check in CI over the token combinations
expected_fix_hints: Adjust the palette step the failing semantic token resolves to
Add a CI contrast gate over token pairings
absent_signals: Do not fix only the one reported screen
Do not rely on visual judgment instead of computing the ratio

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Compute WCAG 2.1 contrast ratios for each text/background pair against the AA floor (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large).
Surfaces this expected flag: Both example pairs likely fail AA for normal text; darken the gray / deepen the button background or shift label.
Surfaces this expected flag: Fix at the semantic-token level so the correction propagates everywhere.
Surfaces this expected flag: Add an automated AA check in CI over the token combinations.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Adjust the palette step the failing semantic token resolves to.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Add a CI contrast gate over token pairings.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not fix only the one reported screen.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not rely on visual judgment instead of computing the ratio.

cases.scenario: Component code references colors directly as gray-50, gray-900, red-700, and blue-600. The brand is about to refresh its red and shift its blue, and the team fears a large code change.
cases.context: The system must survive a brand refresh and support a future dark theme.
cases.question: What should the agent recommend?
expected_flags: Introduce a semantic-token layer named by intent (background-surface, text-primary, danger-emphasis, accent)
Components consume semantic tokens; only the per-theme mapping resolves them to palette values
A brand red shift then changes the mapping, not component code
Names by intent / contrast pair, never by appearance
expected_fix_hints: Define semantic tokens and repoint component references to them
Keep the raw palette as the value vocabulary behind the mapping
absent_signals: Do not keep appearance-named colors in component code
Do not hardcode the new brand red in every component

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Introduce a semantic-token layer named by intent (background-surface, text-primary, danger-emphasis, accent).

cases.scenario: A team is adding a dark theme. Several semantic tokens (border-subtle, text-muted) exist only in the light theme map; the dark theme falls back to undefined or inherits light values, producing invisible borders and low-contrast muted text.
cases.context: The color system already has a light theme and uses semantic tokens.
cases.question: How should the agent ensure parity?
expected_flags: Every semantic token must exist in both themes — no token is light-only or dark-only
Each token's dark resolution must meet the same contrast requirement against its dark surface
The same component token resolves to different palette values per theme (e.g. text near-black on light, near-white on dark)
Verify all interactive-state colors (focus, hover, selected) are visible and AA-compliant in dark
expected_fix_hints: Fill in the missing dark-theme mappings for every semantic token
Re-run the contrast check against dark surfaces
absent_signals: Do not let dark inherit light token values
Do not leave any semantic token unmapped in a theme

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Every semantic token must exist in both themes — no token is light-only or dark-only.
Surfaces this expected flag: Each token's dark resolution must meet the same contrast requirement against its dark surface.
Surfaces this expected flag: The same component token resolves to different palette values per theme (e.g. text near-black on light, near-white on dark).
Surfaces this expected flag: Verify all interactive-state colors (focus, hover, selected) are visible and AA-compliant in dark.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Fill in the missing dark-theme mappings for every semantic token.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Re-run the contrast check against dark surfaces.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not let dark inherit light token values.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not leave any semantic token unmapped in a theme.

cases.scenario: A status system shows success/error/warning purely by color: a green dot vs a red dot vs an amber dot, with no other differentiator. A user reports they cannot tell the states apart.
cases.context: The product serves a broad audience and must be accessible.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the state encoding?
expected_flags: Color must not be the only signal — ~8% of men have color vision deficiency
Pair each state with an icon and/or text label in addition to color
Preview the palette under simulated protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia and confirm distinctions survive
Keep the semantic intent tokens (success/danger/warning) but add a redundant channel
expected_fix_hints: Add distinct icons and/or text to each status
Run a color-blindness simulation pass over the states
absent_signals: Do not rely on hue alone to distinguish states
Do not just pick 'more different' colors as the only fix

cases.scenario: A PM asks the color-system-design owner to implement the dark-mode toggle UI, persist the choice in localStorage, and kill the white flash that dark-mode users see on load.
cases.context: The team conflates 'color' with all theme-related work.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: The toggle UI, persistence, and flash-of-incorrect-theme fix are out of scope — that is dark-mode-implementation
Offer the in-scope part: the contrast-correct dark palette and the semantic-token dark mappings
May note theme-system-design owns the token resolution architecture
Correctly redirects rather than building the runtime mechanics
expected_fix_hints: Hand the runtime switch/persistence/flash work to dark-mode-implementation
Deliver the dark-theme token mappings that the switch will consume
absent_signals: Do not implement the prefers-color-scheme detection or localStorage persistence here
Do not write the inline anti-flash script

cases.scenario: A brand wants a vivid green accent that looks dull in the product; the chosen sRGB green is at the edge of the sRGB gamut and cannot get more saturated.
cases.context: Most of the audience uses modern displays that support display-p3.
cases.question: How should the agent deliver the more saturated color safely?
expected_flags: display-p3 allows more saturated colors than sRGB in the green/red regions
Deliver the p3 color via a p3 color function or color-gamut: p3 declaration
Provide an sRGB fallback so sRGB-only displays still render correctly
Keep the value behind a semantic token so consumers don't hardcode it
expected_fix_hints: Declare the accent in oklch()/p3 with an sRGB fallback
Route it through the accent semantic token
absent_signals: Do not ship a p3 color with no sRGB fallback
Do not assume sRGB can reach the desired saturation
